page: Amazon Web Services r4.8xlarge is a memory-optimized fourth-generation instance powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, supported by a 45 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 244.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.62 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% category. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show weak performance in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all ranking in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with PassMark memory scores, consistently register in the average tier.

Given its high memory capacity and average multi-core capabilities, the r4.8xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not rely heavily on single-thread CPU speed. Appropriate workloads include database operations, Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded data processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of RAM relative to compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound applications, though its older Intel Xeon architecture presents a performance-per-core tradeoff compared to newer hardware generations.
